description_en: The Bāleśvara Mandira stands on a small hill, one kilometre south of Dhuleśvara Śivaji Mahādev Mandir (DLK0330) and 1.5 kilometres to the north of Dullu Bajār.The temple, also called Bāleśvara Śīvālaya, consists in a square structure of 4 x 4 metres, with one single room, accessed by a door to the south. The entrance is preceeded by two circular platforms. A pole is installed in each of them, and changed every year, on the first day of the greatDasaĩ. The first metre of wall elevation is built with cut stones. Above it, the walls and domed ceiling are built out of bricks. On the facades, the stone sections are painted in pink/orange and the upper, brick parts, are whitewashed.At the centre of the temple is a square stand made of bricks, on which is installed a stone disc and a stoneśivaliṅga. Outside, a low platform runs along the temple's walls. On it is installed, to the right side of the door, an inscribed stele dated of ŚS 1277 (1355 CE) (DLK0340_I).Next to one of the two poles is a medieval stone memorial pillar from circa 14th century (DLK0340-001). The pillar is set upside down.A modern altar is built to the south-west of the temple. It contains various little stone artefacts, of which the most noticable is a damaged Buddha statue (DLK0340-002). Dilli Raj Sharma proposed to date the sculpture from the last quarter of the 11th century (Sharma 2012, 46-47). The statue can be roughly dated from the 11th-14th century. It is locally worshiped as a form of Devī (Lecomte-Tilouine 2009). The condition of the statue can be related to other Buddhist images found in the Dullu area, who all show traces of iconoclastic vandalism (seeDLK0200).Acoording to local informants, the monument was built in the first half of the 19th, by Jang Bahadur Bal Kunwar (Jung Bahadur Rana) (Lecomte-Tilouine 2009), when he was a captain.The dome of the temple is in a dire condition.
monument_assessment: Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages), Surface damages, Structural damages
identified_threats: Plants, Water damages, Wall cracks, Erosion

historical_events.event_description: An stele inscribed in Nāgarī script is installed on the right side of the temple's door.Bishwo Pokharel recently published the following reading of the inscription (Pokharel 2011):1. oṁ maṇi padme huṁ2. ālokastimire vipaddibamaṇiḥ pāte ka3. rālambanaṁ yācñākalpatarurjagajjayaratheḥ4. pātheyamanne(nnaṁ)pathi | duḥkhavyādhimahaubadhirbha5. vabhayod vedāntaprayāṇāsanaṃ tāpe  candanakā6. nanaṃ sthirasuhadbhargstatāṃ bāndhavaḥ ||...||7. narakapatitāssatvāṃḥ sukhāvatiṃ modatu || a8. nena puṇyakuśalena | jaisiṃdhena vinirmitāyam9. śrīśāke 1277
